title: MarkMyWords RBI Grade B descriptive rubric
disclaimer: This is MarkMyWords' own framework for RBI Grade B Phase II descriptive answers (typed). RBI does not publish a criterion-wise rubric. It has not yet been calibrated against human expert evaluators.
changelog: 0.1.0 — initial draft for ESI and Finance & Management descriptive answers. Status: calibrating (no calibration report attached).

criteria.name: Question demand & directive
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Judge whether every part of the question is answered and whether the answer does what the directive asks (explain, analyse, evaluate, suggest). RBI questions often pair a concept with an application or policy part — both must be answered. Do not reward length.

bands.descriptor: Does not engage with what the question asks.
Addresses the topic but misses most parts or misreads the directive.
common_failures: defines a concept when asked to apply it

bands.descriptor: Answers some parts; directive partly followed.
common_failures: no recommendation when one is asked

bands.descriptor: Answers all parts; directive followed with minor gaps.
Answers every part with balanced depth and fully performs the directive.
indicators: explicit judgement or recommendation where asked

criteria.name: Conceptual accuracy & coverage
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Reward correct use of economic, financial and management concepts (definitions, frameworks, regulations) and coverage of the dimensions that matter for THIS question — macroeconomic, regulatory, institutional, social, organisational. A list of loosely related terms is not a strength.

bands.descriptor: Concepts absent or wrong.
One relevant concept, thinly or imprecisely explained.
Core concepts correct; important dimensions missing.
common_failures: misses the regulatory or organisational angle

bands.descriptor: Concepts correct and most relevant dimensions covered.
Concepts precise and well chosen; relevant dimensions covered with depth.

criteria.name: Analysis & application
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Reward explanation of how and why (transmission channels, incentives, trade-offs), application of theory to the situation in the question, and a reasoned conclusion or recommendation. Assertions without reasoning are not analysis.

bands.descriptor: Pure assertion; no reasoning.
States outcomes without explaining how they arise.
Some reasoning; theory not applied to the case, or one-sided.
Clear mechanisms and application; conclusion present but thin.
common_failures: recommendation not tied to the analysis

bands.descriptor: Mechanisms, trade-offs and application explained; conclusion follows from the analysis.

criteria.name: Data, examples & accuracy
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Reward accurate, relevant data and references (RBI reports and circulars, Economic Survey, Union Budget, committee reports, laws, recognised management frameworks) and concrete examples. A factual error affects this criterion only and must be cited from the provided sources; otherwise mark it unverifiable.

bands.descriptor: No substantiation, or substantiation that is wrong.
Generic examples only, or a significant factual error.
Some specific evidence; gaps or minor inaccuracies.
Specific, accurate evidence for most claims.
Precise, current and well-chosen evidence supporting the key claims.

criteria.name: Structure & flow
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Typed answers: judge FUNCTION, not template. Does the opening define or frame, does the body move logically (short paragraphs or sub-headings help a reader scan), does the end conclude or recommend? Unconventional structures that do these things are not penalised.

bands.descriptor: No discernible organisation.
Loose organisation; no framing or ending.
Recognisable organisation; framing or conclusion weak.
Frames, progresses and concludes, with minor flow issues.
Clear framing, logical progression and a conclusion that adds a judgement or way forward.

criteria.name: Precision, language & word discipline
criteria.notes_for_evaluator: Clarity, concision and correct terminology in typed prose. RBI descriptive answers carry word limits (about 400 words for 10 marks and 600 for 15 marks); word-limit status is computed by code. Never comment harshly on grammar; flag only what impairs meaning or wastes words.

bands.descriptor: Meaning frequently unclear.
Wordy or imprecise; meaning sometimes unclear.
Clear but wordy or loose with terms.
Clear and mostly concise; terms used correctly.
Crisp, precise and economical.
